items.resolution: Every state tile in the verification showcase section carries a visible text label naming its state, so two states that happen to render identically (e.g. default vs focus on a component without a focus ring) remain distinguishable to the human signer.
items.probe: When two things are exactly equal or just touch, do they merge, collide, or separate?

items.resolution: A component with no applicable interactive state renders only the tiles for the states it actually supports; the section emits no empty placeholder tile for an inapplicable state.
items.probe: What is the result for empty, single-element, or null input?

items.resolution: The eight components appear in a fixed declared order, and within each component the state tiles appear in the fixed order default -> hover -> press -> focus -> disabled, so sign-off captures are positionally comparable across the three themes.
items.probe: When elements compare equal, is output order specified and stable?

items.resolution: At least one sign-off pass runs at a DPI scale strictly different from 100%, and the exact scale used is recorded in the sign-off artifact.
items.probe: What happens exactly at each min/max/threshold — and one step either side?

items.resolution: The sign-off artifact records a separate verdict line per theme (AeroBlue, AeroDark, Classic); no theme's verdict is carried over from or derived from another theme's.
items.probe: When two things are exactly equal or just touch, do they merge, collide, or separate?

items.resolution: The sign-off artifact contains a capture for all three themes; a missing capture is recorded as a FAIL, never treated as an implicit pass.
items.probe: What is the result for empty, single-element, or null input?

items.resolution: The human sign-off runs only after the mechanical gates and code review are green (D-03 ordering). If a sign-off verdict predates the gates going green, that verdict is void and must be re-run.
items.probe: When elements compare equal, is output order specified and stable?

items.resolution: The recorded DPI scale is an exact stated value (e.g. 150%), not a range or an approximation such as 'above 100%'.
items.probe: Where can precision loss, overflow, or rounding/tie-breaking occur — and what is the exact contract (e.g. half-up vs half-to-even, ceil/floor/truncate)?

items.resolution: The gate flags a pixel literal used as a gradient stop coordinate but does not flag an unrelated numeric literal appearing in an adjacent argument on the same source line.
items.probe: When two things are exactly equal or just touch, do they merge, collide, or separate?

items.resolution: A source file containing zero gradient call sites passes the gate cleanly; an empty scan set is a pass, not an error and not a vacuous failure.
items.probe: What is the result for empty, single-element, or null input?

items.resolution: The gate scans comment-stripped source via the existing nonCommentSource helper, so a pixel literal such as endY = 100f discussed inside KDoc or a line comment neither raises a false positive nor masks a real violation.
items.probe: Whose definition of length/equality applies — bytes, code points, grapheme clusters, or normalized form?

items.resolution: When multiple violations exist the gate's failure message enumerates every offending file and call site, so fixing them in any order cannot hide a remaining violation behind a first-failure abort.
items.probe: When elements compare equal, is output order specified and stable?

items.resolution: A file containing both a .clip(...) and an .aeroSurface(...) in separate, unrelated modifier chains passes the gate; only a .clip(...) applied after .aeroSurface(...) within the same chain is a violation. AeroSegmentedControl.kt is the concrete case this must not flag.
items.probe: When two things are exactly equal or just touch, do they merge, collide, or separate?

items.resolution: A source file with zero aeroSurface( call sites passes the gate cleanly rather than erroring or vacuously failing.
items.probe: What is the result for empty, single-element, or null input?

items.resolution: The gate scans comment-stripped source via the existing nonCommentSource helper, so the literal .clip() appearing in AeroButtonSurface.kt's KDoc prose does not trigger a violation.
items.probe: Whose definition of length/equality applies — bytes, code points, grapheme clusters, or normalized form?

items.resolution: The gate is order-sensitive within a modifier chain: .aeroSurface(...).clip(...) fails and .clip(...).aeroSurface(...) passes. Order-insensitive substring matching is not sufficient to satisfy this requirement.
items.probe: When elements compare equal, is output order specified and stable?

items.resolution: Each measured default size and corner radius is asserted exactly equal to its v2.0.4 baseline value; a deviation of one dp in either direction fails the test.
items.probe: What happens exactly at each min/max/threshold — and one step either side?

items.resolution: Two components whose baseline values happen to coincide (e.g. both 4.dp corner radius) are asserted independently and keyed by component identity, so a swap between them cannot pass.
items.probe: When two things are exactly equal or just touch, do they merge, collide, or separate?

items.resolution: The test asserts a non-zero expected count of measured components; an empty measurement set fails rather than trivially passing.
items.probe: What is the result for empty, single-element, or null input?

items.resolution: Measurements are keyed by component identity rather than by list position, so reordering the components under test does not change the verdict.
items.probe: When elements compare equal, is output order specified and stable?

items.resolution: Dp values are compared by exact equality against the baseline constant, not with a float tolerance, so sub-dp rounding drift cannot be silently absorbed.
items.probe: Where can precision loss, overflow, or rounding/tie-breaking occur — and what is the exact contract (e.g. half-up vs half-to-even, ceil/floor/truncate)?

items.resolution: Both converted buttons are asserted separately; a single shared assertion that could pass with only one of the two buttons wired is not sufficient.
items.probe: When two things are exactly equal or just touch, do they merge, collide, or separate?

items.resolution: The test fails if the button under test is absent from the semantics tree, rather than passing vacuously on a missing node.
items.probe: What is the result for empty, single-element, or null input?

items.resolution: The verdict does not depend on the order in which the two buttons are exercised; each button's activation is asserted in its own isolated composition.
items.probe: When elements compare equal, is output order specified and stable?

items.resolution: Pressing the activation key twice invokes the click handler twice; the test asserts the invocation count, not merely that the handler was invoked at least once.
items.probe: What happens if this runs twice on the same input?

items.resolution: Key-event delivery interleaved with a recomposition in the same frame is not asserted — runComposeUiTest drives a single-threaded test clock, so real-device input/recomposition races remain outside this test's reach.
items.probe: If interrupted or run in parallel, what is guaranteed?

items.resolution: The scratch consumer declares the library by its published coordinate and version; it must not resolve the library through includeBuild or project substitution against this repository, which would prove the source tree rather than the artifact.
items.probe: When two things are exactly equal or just touch, do they merge, collide, or separate?

items.resolution: The scratch consumer imports nothing from the showcase module and uses only the library's public API surface; a consumer that compiles only because it borrowed a showcase helper does not satisfy VER-05.
items.probe: What is the result for empty, single-element, or null input?

items.resolution: All eight components render in the consumer regardless of the order they are declared in the consumer's composable; render order independence is confirmed by visual inspection, not by an automated assertion.
items.probe: When elements compare equal, is output order specified and stable?

items.resolution: The consumer build resolves the artifact with a refreshed dependency cache, so a previously cached older artifact cannot satisfy the new coordinate and produce a false pass.
items.probe: If interrupted or run in parallel, what is guaranteed?

items.resolution: Each gate's broken fixture differs from its clean fixture by exactly the one property that gate checks, so the red verdict is attributable to that property and nothing else.
items.probe: When two things are exactly equal or just touch, do they merge, collide, or separate?

items.resolution: A gate carrying zero fixtures fails the VER-06 proof; every new gate must ship both a violating fixture and a clean fixture.
items.probe: What is the result for empty, single-element, or null input?

items.resolution: Each gate's proof asserts red-on-broken-fixture and green-on-clean-fixture, and both assertions live in the same test class so neither can be run or pass in isolation.
items.probe: When elements compare equal, is output order specified and stable?

items.resolution: Running the proof twice yields the same verdict; fixtures are in-file constants per D-08, so no fixture file is mutated or left behind between runs.
items.probe: What happens if this runs twice on the same input?

items.resolution: Fixtures are in-file string constants and are never written into the source tree, so a parallel or interrupted test run cannot leave deliberately-broken code committed in the repository.
items.probe: If interrupted or run in parallel, what is guaranteed?
